title: Columbia Workshop
paragraphs: CBS's influential experimental anthology, created as a laboratory for radio drama and known for unusual scripts, literary adaptations, music, narration, and inventive use of sound.
CBS sustaining experimental anthology and radio-drama laboratory.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Original experimental run (July 18, 1936 to November 8, 1942) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], Postwar revival (February 2, 1946 to January 25, 1947) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and Once Upon a Tune continuation (February 1, 1947 to April 26, 1947) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Norman Corwin (director, writer, and producer), William N. Robson (director, producer, and radio adaptor), Bernard Herrmann (conductor, composer, and music), [[person|frank-lovejoy|Frank Lovejoy]] (performer), Alexander Semmler (conductor, composer, and arranger), Earle McGill (director, host, and performer), and Irving Reis (director, producer, and writer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], [[org|org.d99a6af306cbccd9|WBNS]], [[org|org.7027e8a3676e0d84|KNX]], [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]], and [[org|org.b1c76a6702c1bee9|WABC]].
The stories often return to literature and literary adaptation, radio experimentation, music and sound, war and conflict, science and technology, and crime and violence.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Network radio as an experimental dramatic art, Experimental broadcast sound techniques, and Postwar revival of experimental network drama.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], and [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]].
